description:
Most people are scared of margin because they think margin investing means margin calls, forced liquidation, and blowing up a portfolio.

I think about it differently.

In this video, I break down how I use margin as a disciplined business tool inside the Paycheck to Portfolio system. I’m not using margin to gamble, chase meme stocks, or treat my brokerage account like free money. I use margin the way a business owner thinks about working capital, cash flow, capital allocation, equity growth, borrowing cost, and return on capital.

The goal is simple:

Bring income into the brokerage.
Invest into assets.
Build equity.
Create dividend cash flow.
Use margin strategically to stay fully invested.
Manage the portfolio like a business.

Most people spend their paycheck, pay bills, and start over from zero every month.

I don’t.

I bring my income into the brokerage account first. That money helps pay down margin, increases equity, and gives the portfolio more strength. Then I use margin as a line of credit against the portfolio so my assets can continue working instead of constantly pulling money back out.

In this video, I walk through my real brokerage account, current portfolio update, E*TRADE margin tab, available for withdrawal, Reg-T margin, portfolio margin, margin maintenance requirements, dividend income, margin interest, and the cash flow spread that powers the system.

I also explain one of the most misunderstood parts of margin investing:

When $5,000 comes into the brokerage, it can pay down margin and increase equity by $5,000. But once that equity is redeployed, it does not work like a checking account. Margin maintenance determines how much equity is required to support the position. That is why a brokerage account can start to function more like a business balance sheet than a normal savings account.

This is where people get confused.

They think it is just moving money around.

It’s not.

It is converting income into productive capital.

Cash flow matters.
Margin cost matters.
Maintenance requirements matter.
Equity growth matters most.

I also cover why I use Reg-T margin instead of portfolio margin, how I think about 30%, 50%, and 100% margin maintenance requirements, why dividend income can help cover margin interest, and why I treat my portfolio more like real estate or a business than a pile of random stocks.

The goal is not to max out margin.

The goal is to build a portfolio like a business.

If you have ever wondered how margin works, how to borrow against your portfolio, how Reg-T margin works, how margin maintenance affects buying power, how dividend income can cover margin interest, or how to build a portfolio that creates cash flow and equity over time, this video is for you.

Equity creates wealth.
Cash flow supports the system.
Margin is just a tool.
